# Results summary (generated by analysis/plot.py)

## 2 players

| Case | RTT mean (ms) | RTT p95 (ms) | Jitter (ms) | Loss down (%) | Loss up (%) | Snapshots/s | Finished | Timeouts | iperf got (Mbit/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No congestion | 7.2 | 12.6 | 2.9 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 20.0 | 2 / 2 | 0 | - |
| Congested, no SDN (baseline) | 89.1 | 119.7 | 19.3 | 0.3 | 0.0 | 19.8 | 2 / 2 | 0 | 9.0 |
| Congested, static priority | 5.3 | 6.9 | 2.3 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 19.9 | 2 / 2 | 0 | 8.8 |
| Congested, dynamic SDN | 13.5 | 81.6 | 4.1 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 19.9 | 2 / 2 | 0 | 8.9 |

**Dynamic SDN vs no SDN under the same congestion:** RTT p95 119.7 ms -> 81.6 ms (1.5 times lower); downlink loss 0.3 % -> 0.0 %; snapshots/s 19.8 -> 19.9; players finished 2 -> 2 of 2; controller reaction time 2.1 s.

**Dynamic vs static priority:** RTT p95 81.6 ms vs 6.9 ms; the controller kept priority on for 73 % of the polls (static: always); background iperf got 8.9 vs 8.8 Mbit/s.

## SDN verification (did the traffic really use the priority queue?)

| Case | Players | Packets in game queue 1 | Packets in other queue 0 | Priority flows on s1 during the race | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No congestion | 2 | 0 | 1681 | 0 | ok |
| Congested, no SDN (baseline) | 2 | 0 | 28255 | 0 | ok |
| Congested, static priority | 2 | 1656 | 23875 | 4 | ok |
| Congested, dynamic SDN | 2 | 1196 | 23961 | 4 | ok |
| No congestion | 4 | 0 | 3374 | 0 | ok |
| Congested, no SDN (baseline) | 4 | 0 | 38295 | 0 | ok |
| Congested, static priority | 4 | 3537 | 27218 | 8 | ok |
| Congested, dynamic SDN | 4 | 2356 | 25849 | 8 | ok |
| No congestion | 8 | 0 | 7199 | 0 | ok |
| Congested, no SDN (baseline) | 8 | 0 | 40301 | 0 | ok |
| Congested, static priority | 8 | 7154 | 27354 | 16 | ok |
| Congested, dynamic SDN | 8 | 5040 | 27249 | 16 | ok |

The packet counts are read from the bottleneck port of s1 after the race (`verify.txt`). The check passes when the game queue carried the game's packets in the cases with priority and stayed unused in the cases without. The priority flows are the `set_queue:1` rules counted about 10 s after the congestion starts (`flows_in_race.txt`); with `--match registered` there are two per player address, one for each direction. '-' means that the run has no such sample. After the race the switch holds none, because the controller removes a player's rules when the player leaves.

Notes: loss and jitter are measured only while the race is running. 'Loss down' comes from the packet sequence numbers and cannot see a total blackout; 'Snapshots/s' can (a silent player receives 0). Values are means over the repetitions of each case.
